title: A list's per-element count agrees with its computed multiset's count
statement: For any element a and list l over Nat, the number of times a occurs in l (List.count) equals the multiplicity Nat.Multiset assigns to a in the multiset built by folding l (List.toMultiset) -- the new ordinary-inductive List carrier and the earlier function-plus-bound Nat.Multiset carrier (ADR-1520) agree on how many times a value occurs.

formal.statement: theorem List.count_toMultiset : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : List.{0} AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (List.count x0 x1) (AxNat.Multiset.count (List.toMultiset x1) x0)))

evidence.supports: List.count_toMultiset is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example list_theorem_inventory -- List.count_toMultiset 2>/dev/null | grep -Fc '((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : List.{0} AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (List.count x0 x1) (AxNat.Multiset.count (List.toMultiset x1) x0)))')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: The pattern is the FULL admitted type (rendered by Kernel::render_lean via list_theorem_inventory), not the theorem's name -- a drifted statement would fail this check. This theorem was recorded as NOT landed by list-carrier-1 (docs/plan/status/460-list-carrier-1.md); list-carrier-2 found the blocker it named -- a beq-to-ne bridge lemma -- was unnecessary, since Nat.Multiset.count_singleton_of_ne is already stated directly in terms of beq.

evidence.notes: count_to_multiset_landed_axiom_free_and_matches_concretely instantiates the theorem at (a:=1, l:=[1,2,1]) and (a:=3, l:=[1,2,1]), checks Kernel::infer succeeds at both, and confirms count 1 [1,2,1] = 2 (not 0) and count 3 [1,2,1] = 0 (not 2) by def_eq.

provenance.source: theorem name and canonical type read directly via list_theorem_inventory, which prints render_lean of the admitted type; declared by list_prelude/bridge.rs (lane list-carrier-2, ADR-1583 amending ADR-1579).

notes: Induction on l, a fixed. The nil case is Nat.Multiset.count_eq_zero_of_bound_le at Nat.Multiset.zero (bound zero is 0 by iota, so Nat.zero_le a already has the type its hypothesis wants). The cons case case-splits on Nat.beq head a (a fresh Bool.rec-based Or split, since nat_prelude's own copy of that helper is not visible outside nat_prelude): the true branch transports head = a (Nat.eq_of_beq_eq_true) through Nat.Multiset.count_singleton_self; the false branch flips the hypothesis via Nat.beq_comm and applies Nat.Multiset.count_singleton_of_ne directly (which is already stated in terms of beq, not Not (Eq _ _), so no separate ne-bridge lemma was needed).
